Knowledge tracing is an area of research that focuses on several key questions, one of which is trying to predict a student's current proficiency based their current history. Many deep learning based methods have been proposed in this field, yet comparing these models' performances has been inconsistent due to the lack of a common evaluation framework. To fill this gap, we present pyKT, a Python library that standardizes the assessment of deep learning based knowledge tracing models by unifying data formats and re-implementing key algorithms. We demonstrate pyKT's capabilities with two case studies using the EduGene and ITKET datasets. Our hope is that pyKT provides a consistent evaluation framework for the knowledge tracing community and stimulates further high-quality research in this field.

Given any smooth vector field $V$ on a real algebraic variety $X$ within a Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$, we establish that it has closed range with respect to $L^2$ functions, provided $V$ is elliptic on its domain. This confirmation implies the solvability of the equation $\dv f = \gamma$ under certain conditions, also implying that on any compact variety $X$, there's a smooth coisometry $J$ such that $\dv (J \gamma) = \gamma$ holds for all $L^2$ functions $\gamma$.

Seven years ago, Leuze, de Ruiter and Botteiller introduced the Alethee project, 
whose goal is to create a universal SMT argument format and accompanying tools. 
This format and toolset enable automatic verification proofs that rely on 
intermediate languages like CaLP and Coq, utilizing modern SMT solvers. 
Our refined approach expands the initial A-theory acronym to represent accuracy, 
uniformity, and reliability, also addressing efficiency in our design.

As federated learning (FL) expands for its real-world applications, challenges arise from the computational complexities involved in syncing clients and conducting secure model updates. In many FL settings, confidential asynchronous aggregation techniques have been prevalent due to their adaptability. Nonetheless, limited research has addressed the algorithmic constraints on gradient updates in this context. This study aims to break these limitations, particularly those related to variance-increasing asynchronous updates. A novel asynchronous update protocol is proposed, enabling agents to participate in multiple rounds of learning without risking convergence difficulties. The proposed method's theoretical guarantees are established across various distributed optimization algorithms. Furthermore, our asynchronous FL approach demonstrates improved performance in both theory and testing compared to existing techniques.

Recently, an end-to-lightning transcription model was proposed that achieves superior performance by effectively utilizing large-scale multilingual pre-trained models. To further enhance this model's performance, this article investigates two data set adaptation techniques: customizing the attention mechanism and transferring knowledge across language barriers. Our experimental results show this model's advantage over traditional micro-parametric ASR transfer methods, while also demonstrating that modifying the attention mechanism yields significant improvements. Furthermore, our results indicate that utilizing English labels as intermediate guides can benefit non-English transcription tasks.

Our proposed RL model, based on Sparse Gaussian Process TD learning, shows superior performance in marine robot guidance. Traditional policy gradient methods rely on sample-based function approximation, which can be computationally intensive for intricate environments. In contrast, our non-linear model provides a compact representation of state-action values and yields faster reinforcement learning. Moreover, our sparse architecture enables efficient policy evaluation and update, consuming significantly less memory and processing time. Experimental results show that our model achieves convergence with a smaller number of experiences, while also demonstrating superior performance and efficient guidance on an underwater vehicle.

We employ a 1+1+2 covariant framework to investigate dual-fluid anisotropic stellar configurations within the context of General Relativity, utilizing the Tolman IV static and spherically symmetric metric as our baseline. By integrating the Tolman IV metric with two interacting, anisotropic dual-fluid fields, we establish that it fulfills the corresponding Einstein field equations. Through this process, we derive expressions for mass-to-energy ratios in the form of series expansions, both of which are expandable around the object's central point and its outer boundary respectively. These expansions are essential for determining the objects' total masses. Furthermore, we develop 1+1+2 covariant stability criteria specifically tailored to two anisotropic dual-fluid objects, which also facilitate the calculation of their total masses. However, calculating mass integrals directly proves cumbersome; hence, we propose a numerical approach based on the object's radial coordinates to compute mass integrals and thereby its total mass. Our numerical results for mass-to-radius ratios are presented in the form of graphs, along with corresponding fit equations for easy reference. We also plot stability regions in the form of radial proportionations to provide a clear visual representation of our 1+1+2 covariant stability criteria. In addition, we present examples utilizing realistic compact object equations of state to demonstrate how our theoretical framework can be applied to concrete scenarios, complete with outer boundary conditions and outer surface densities and pressures in the form of list equations for easy reference.

Most current sequence-based grammatical error correction (GEC) models struggle to generalize to new domains with limited data, requiring extensive domain adaptation that necessitates access to target domain data. In contrast, this paper presents a novel approach using meta-learning to transfer knowledge across domains, creating a domain-transfer GEC model that only needs source domain data. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach on the Li & Tetreault (2017) corpus, showing significant improvements in F scores when evaluating on low LiDAR datasets. Our results indicate a notable performance of this approach when compared to strong baselines, achieving an average improvement of 5.3 points in F scores. To validate our hypothesis, we conducted ablation studies that examined the relevance of meta-learning and the choice of loss functions in this context.

This paper investigates the challenges of achieving fairness in settings where multiple agents, free to act selfishly, must allocate indivisible goods without any goods being given up, and provides an analysis of whether concepts of fairness, such as envy-freeness up to one good (EF1) and low levels of envy (α-ENV for some constant α), can be guaranteed. We initially establish that for agents with utilitarian preferences, there is always a strategy profile where the total utility of all agents is maximized, and at least one agent's utility is at least as high as the highest possible utility of any single good for each agent. Furthermore, we determine that it is possible to efficiently find the indivisible goods allocation corresponding to these high-total-utility, low-level-envy, and ef1 equilibria. In contrast, for agents with satiable preferences, we demonstrate that it is not always possible to guarantee an allocation that simultaneously maximizes total utility and minimizes envy for some constant α < 1.

UGC 8839 is an exceptionally rare, extremely faint, low surface brightness dwarf galaxy noted for its unusual characteristics. Despite being almost entirely neutral in gas composition, the galaxy shows rapid star formation occurring in a very narrow ring, only about 1.5 kiloparsecs in diameter, within its peripheral regions. In contrast, the central 3.5 kiloparsecs has very few stars that have formed recently. This highly fragmented distribution of stars, combined with the galaxy's low overall density, has led to a stable, high-eccentricity disk structure that has persisted for a long period. A theoretical model suggesting that galaxies like this one, which are very dark and lack a prominent bulge, could make up a significant portion of the universe's total matter could be supported by the discovery of UGC 8839's behavior.

Using lattice QCD, the associations of two-type currents within a pion are examined, with the current types being flavor and spin. The lattice results are compared to theoretical predictions from chiral perturbation theory and change with respect to the quark mass analyzed. Findings demonstrate that the association of two flavor currents aligns with χPT predictions, yet a discrepancy exists between lattice results concerning the association of two spin currents and χPT predictions at low quark masses. Evidence suggests that the association of a spin and a flavor current within a pion does not match the χPT prediction of a bar one-half. Additionally, the ratios of two-current associations to the square of the charge radius and two-point correlations are calculated on the lattice, revealing interesting results regarding spin currents in comparison to flavor currents within a pion.

Protoplanetary disks are thought to contribute to the formation of planets by undergoing gas accretion and planet formation processes. However, there is currently no straightforward way to predict these processes due in part to uncorrelated observations made at different points in time and across various parts of the system. A significant issue arises from this lack of predictability, as it can lead to unrealistic accuracy in accretion rates near important regions, such as inner disk, surface, and planets. To address this challenge, a new, more consistent method is proposed that involves simultaneously measuring multiple parts of the system at the same time. Using a prominent dust continuum source known as XX Cha as an example, its unusual accretion variability with a short timescale of a few days is revealed in spectrum observations. As a result of this discovery, the short timescale of accretion variability in XX Cha is found to produce an extensive range of short-term accretion rates. As evidence, the spread in best-fit accretion rates found in different observations is found to directly reflect the range of short-term accretion rates found in spectrum observations. As a result, the wide spread in best-fit accretion rates found in different observations is found to directly reflect the range of short-term accretion rates found in the data. As a result, the spread in estimated accretion rates found in different observations is found to directly reflect the range of short-term accretion rates found in the data.

In offline single-agent reinforcement learning, an agent's policy evaluation and improvement can be freely carried out given an unbiased state value function. However, in offline multi-agent settings, these actions are limited by the need for joint trajectories to be within the support of the underlying independent policies. We investigate this oversight and extend the single-agent framework by introducing two novel offline multi-agent problems, requiring algorithms that derive value functions from independent data and policies. Firstly, we propose an evaluation phase where an algorithm interacts with the true underlying independent policies to collect joint trajectories. Secondly, we develop an iterative improvement stage where policies are refined in pairs. We present a novel algorithm that guarantees an $\epsilon$-Nash Equilibrium outcome with a sample size of $\tilde{O}\left(\frac{SA^2(\log A)^2}{\epsilon}\right).$ Furthermore, we explore the practical applicability of this theoretical approach through real-world experiments.

We developed a novel approach to align Megavoltage images using Convolutional Neural Networks in both 2D and 3D. Our method utilizes deep learning to capture complex relationships in image data for accurate radiation tumor targeting. To compare our results, we utilized a popular Alignement Field method and found that our Convolutional Neural Network model achieved comparable translation estimation accuracy. Furthermore, our model demonstrated its versatility by effectively handling CT scans from various sources.

We establish that single-particle entanglement must possess a genuinely nonlocal character by demonstrating that it can lead to single-particle steering, which has been underapposed as such until now. We show this requires falsifying two nonlocality assumptions put forward recently, one of which we do so by creating experimentally verifiable criteria. These criteria can be tested using existing setups and suggest that single-particle entanglement must possess a form of intrinsic nonlocality, which we further explore theoretically.

The integration of Artificial Intelligence techniques and AI-enabled systems within the Internet of Vehicles (IoVs) has gained considerable interest in recent years due to their potential to revolutionize vehicle operations and user experiences. However, this collaboration also poses significant challenges, including those associated with large-scale, decentralized data sharing that compromises data privacy and trust. This paper presents a comprehensive review of Federated Learning frameworks that incorporate Blockchain technology to address these challenges. This review delves into various IoV applications for FL, examines critical challenges and open questions that must be resolved, and highlights potential FL-based solutions that could transform the IoV ecosystem. This review is anticipated to serve as a valuable reference for researchers and practitioners working in the fields of IoV and artificial intelligence.

V392 Persei, recognized as a dwarf nova, underwent one of its most extraordinary events in 2014 when a massive solar explosion occurred. Initially classified as an optical nova, it was later confirmed via radio and X-ray observations to have extended into the gamma-ray spectrum, detected by the Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope. Observations suggest the explosion's source was confined within the inner part of its gamma-ray luminosity sphere, indicating electron acceleration within the wind of the neutron star. Our analysis of the electron population dynamics, guided by general relativistic hydrodynamics, points to a high-brightness spectral energy distribution on the Compton shoulder, potentially observable in the X-ray to radio spectrum. Post-eruption, V392 Persei's spectral energy distribution shifted, with its neutron star accretion disk exposed to intense irradiation, influencing the exterior gas and possibly accounting for observed reflections. Post-eruption, V392 Persei's luminosity declined, with its spectrum characteristic of a stable configuration, albeit with unusually narrow emission lines, indicating slow wind speeds around the neutron star. Based on its location relative to the galactic center and previous observations, we predict a high probability of V392 Persei's observable status within a specific wavelength range, with recent observations supporting this assessment.

A proposed precoder codebook feedback method leverages Type-2 Generative Adversarial Networks to create codebooks and encode user feedback, addressing the limitations of traditional mutual information optimization approaches in this context.

We perform comprehensive calculations of homogeneous surface current densities on a rigorous equilibrium basis, without approximations or mean-field theories, for a 3D hollow square lattice filled with electrons and subjected to a perpendicular magnetic field. Our analysis of the Hofstadter model, including spin degrees of freedom, includes the derivation of an exact level statistics in an infinite lattice and identifies surface current eigenvalues that form a separate sequence within the energy spectrum. Visualizing surface currents reveals robust 2D nonequilibrium patterns in each 3D layer, characterized by local conservation of flux through a detailed layer-to-layer energy spectrum mapping. These surface currents exist in isolated high-energy, spatially localized states, representing a new form of surface localization that arises from 3D geometry rather than dimensionally reduced systems.

In the context of general relativity, by examining the mass conservation law for a fluid that adheres to perfect characteristics, we investigated the maximum possible Bondi mass loss rate for stars in accordance with the Stefan-Boltzmann law of blackbody radiation. Our analysis reveals that the mass loss rate is constrained by a function specifically designed for stars, and we observed that for a star with a small radius, particularly in a vacuum, it could theoretically approach infinity. Furthermore, we applied this constraint to known compact objects, and as a result, we found that for HALEOP-2, JWRE-4320, and JWST-23, they can potentially coexist without conflict. Conversely, we determined that this limitation causes several objects such as 43COP-1908, ROR-1403, and G20-58 to exist in impossible scenarios.

The earliest stars that formed in the universe's first galaxies, which were often located within dense star clusters, could have formed massive black hole remnants.  Our study uses a specialized simulation model to assess the probability of these black hole remnants merging while residing within these star clusters.  The model takes into consideration the characteristics of the earliest stars and provides insights into the types of merging black hole remnants detected by gravitational wave observatories.  The simulation model predicts that detecting black hole mergers from these early stars would require next-generation gravitational wave detectors like Einstein Telescope or Cosmic Explorer.  The detection of such events would have significant implications for our understanding of the first stars and their environments.

In this study, we examine the security risks of a wireless communication system with multiple senders and receivers connected through a single relay on an OFDM network. We compare two methods of transmitting data: one where the relay forwards information it has received and another where it generates new data to forward. We analyze the security threats to this system and determine the levels of cribs and relay keys required to ensure safe communication across all frequency bands. Our findings show that using a crib requires significantly more resources than utilizing a relay key. Our research contributes to the understanding of secure wireless communication systems with a single relay and provides insights into choosing the most effective method of ensuring security.

Text-based games provide a rigorous platform to assess virtual agents in tasks like natural language understanding, solving complex problems, and applying real-world knowledge.
One significant limitation of existing text-based games lies in their slow speed, with execution rates capped around three actions per second.
Our research presents TextWorldExpress, the first text-based game simulation capable of operating at one million actions per second on current hardware, providing a speedup of three orders of magnitude over previous solutions.
To achieve this breakthrough, we developed two key technologies: a highly efficient narrative consistency checker that uses differential parsing to maintain story coherence, and a cutting-edge physics simulation acceleration method.
We released TextWorldExpress along with enhanced versions of two prominent text-based game challenges, allowing for the assessment of super-fast natural language processing models.
Our findings reveal a previous record for environment simulation execution rates, previously thought to be limited around ten thousand actions per second, is actually three times higher, now found to be one million actions per second.

Deep learning models, particularly those based on Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), are highly effective in processing sequential data but suffer from inefficiencies in operation and deployment due to their large size. This challenge is especially pronounced in video analysis applications, which involve processing substantial amounts of data. To address this limitation, our research proposes an integrated algorithm and hardware design for LSTM-based systems that prioritize energy efficiency. Our optimized architecture streamlines data flow management and leverages parallel processing capabilities to achieve significant improvements in performance and energy usage. Our results demonstrate that this integrated design outperforms competitive alternatives by a margin of 5.5 to 84 times in processing speed and 8 to 10 times in energy consumption in addition to offering scalable performance as the size of data sets grows.
